delights: My four walls held everywhere I looked. GET /api/recipes told me "hiddenCount": 687 of 889 recipes removed, and across all 202 that remained I found zero ingredients naming dairy, egg, gluten or soy. Nothing on my plate, and nothing on my shopping list, broke a wall. For a coeliac that is the whole ballgame and this app got it right.
The day adds up. My four slots total 2226 kcal against my 2221 target — 5 kcal off — with 259 g protein, which is exactly the high-protein shape I asked for.

It tells me when it failed instead of pretending: "Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance — closest was "Classic Salmon & Broccoli with Potato" (landed 817 kcal vs a 579 target)." I would much rather be told that than be handed a silent miss.

defects.what: The shopping list is not my plan. It omits the salmon and the chicken — 2 of my 3 main meals — so if I shopped from it I would come home unable to cook dinner or lunch.
defects.snippet: POST /plans/<id>/grocery-list returned 57 items; Salmon and "Chicken breast, cooked, skinless" are both absent, while my plan calls for 300 g and 255 g of them.

defects.what: The same list adds 47 foods I never agreed to eat, including meats and booze that appear nowhere in my day.
defects.snippet: Goat Meat 695 g | Chorizo | Pepperoni | "Ground pack (elk/game), cooked" | Dry White Wine 120 g | Scotch Bonnet | Avocado chips | Jamaican Curry Powder

defects.what: Quantities on the list are wildly larger than the day needs, and the total price is unusable for one day of food for one person.
defects.snippet: Shrimp 1545 g (I need 340 g), Quinoa 1100 g (I need 170 g), Beef jerky 320 g (I need 35 g); "totalEstimatedCostCad": 248.57

defects.what: It admits it cannot tell me how much to actually buy, on every single line. For rice and quinoa cooked-vs-dry is a threefold difference at the till.
defects.snippet: "form": "as-prepared (state unrecorded) — NOT a raw/dry purchase quantity"

defects.what: The list has duplicate and nonsense entries, and one price note tells me, the customer, to go edit a source file.
defects.snippet: "Bay Leaf" (spices) and "Bay Leaves" (other) as two items; "Water" and "Boiling Water" (/usr/bin/bash.92); three oils — "Oil", "Vegetable Oil", "Oil, corn, peanut, and olive"; note: "edit src/lib/groceryPrices.js to correct"

defects.what: Two of the three AI-written dishes are not recipes. I am 74 and I have cooked for fifty years, but this tells a beginner nothing — no heat, no time, no seasoning, no lemon.
defects.snippet: "steps": ["Cook the shrimp.","Serve over quinoa with cucumber."]

defects.what: My vegetables were halved while protein doubled. 55 g of broccoli is about three florets sitting next to a 300 g salmon fillet. When I am cutting, veg is the one thing that should not shrink.
defects.snippet: proteinScale 2, sidesScale 0.5 — Salmon 300 g, Russet Potato 90 g, Broccoli 55 g

defects.what: The snack is beef jerky and pork rinds. At 74 that is leathery, salty and genuinely hard to chew, and it is also the one processed multi-ingredient item on my plan carrying no allergen data at all — commercial jerky is usually marinated in soy sauce, which is both soy and wheat. I would have to stand in the shop reading labels because the app has nothing to tell me.
defects.snippet: "Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate" — Beef jerky 35 g, Pork rinds 17 g; food record shows "allergenTags": null, "mayContain": null

defects.what: I said nothing over 15 minutes to cook and that never got saved, so the 15-minute prep times I got are luck rather than a rule the app is holding to.
My snack slot has effectively one recipe in the entire app once my walls are applied, so there is nothing to swap to.
defects.snippet: "Tried 1 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance"

followUp.action: I did not want the jerky-and-pork-rinds snack — it is hard to chew at my age and it under-delivered protein — so I asked for alternates for that slot, the way a customer would tap "show me something else".
followUp.howItWent: The call worked but offered exactly one alternative, "Pistachios & Jerky", which is more of the very thing I was trying to get away from — 80 g of beef jerky, up from 35 g — and it blows the budget at 412 kcal against a 258 kcal target. I left the original in place because the only option on offer was worse.

verdict: It protected my coeliac and my allergies flawlessly and hit my calorie target within 5 kcal, but the shopping list left out the salmon and the chicken while telling me to buy goat meat and white wine for 48 — so I cannot actually get this day of food into my kitchen.
